title: Aurum Alpha data-export package manifest
description: standards/082-data-subject-rights.md DR3: manifest.json at the root of an export package. It names what the package holds and where it came from, so a recipient can verify every file and a reviewer can compare the package against the inventory that generated it. Every file the zip contains is listed here with its digest; a file not listed is a defect in the builder, and a listed file that is absent is a defect in the delivery. schema_version 1 - evolves additively per PC6.

path.description: rows/<entry>.jsonl for a relational or document entry, rows/<entry>.<subject_column>.jsonl where a store carries two entries, blobs/<entry>/<object public id> for an object. Forward slashes, no absolute paths, no parent references - the zip is opened on a machine the service does not control.

entry.description: The inventory entry the file was built from. The package is a function of the inventory, and this is the join.

count.description: rows only: lines in the file. Zero is legal - an exported entry with no rows for this subject still yields a file, so the recipient can tell 'nothing held' from 'not exported'.

object_id.description: blob only: the object's public id per 026.

filename.description: blob only: the original filename from the object's metadata, for the recipient. Never part of the path, which is the object id.

content_type.description: blob only: the content type the service recorded at upload (026), not one sniffed at export.

request_id.description: The request resource this package answers.

tenant_id.description: DR3: the tenant the package is bounded to.

release.description: The repository version that built the package (010), so a package can be reproduced against the inventory as it was.

inventory_sha256.description: Digest of the inventory declaration the builder read. Two packages built under different inventories differ in ways the file list alone may not show.

row_format.description: One JSON object per line, snake_case keys per 050 HA8, primitives per 020 - a row format a job streams in keyset batches (057 JB7) without holding a table in memory, and a recipient parses with any JSON library.
